C005.subject: free trade agreements
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: free trade agreements developing economies]

[PATH:empirical] Panel data analysis of patent filings and R&D expenditure in ICT firms across ASEAN member states, comparing periods before and after implementation of key FTAs (e.g., ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand FTA, 2010) — Directly tests whether FTA adoption correlates with increased innovation output, controlling for FDI, education, and infrastructure.

[PATH:literature] Case studies of technology transfer clauses in selected FTAs (e.g., US-Singapore FTA, 2004) and their impact on local ICT startup ecosystems in Vietnam and Thailand — Qualitative evidence can reveal causal mechanisms (e.g., IP protection, joint ventures) that quantitative data may miss.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical model: endogenous growth framework incorporating trade liberalization, knowledge spillovers, and absorptive capacity in developing economies — Provides a formal basis to predict conditions under which FTAs enhance or hinder innovation, guiding empirical design.

C006.subject: free trade
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: free trade developing economies]

[PATH:empirical] World Bank Enterprise Surveys on manufacturing firm performance in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, 1990-2020 — Provides firm-level panel data on productivity, output, and employment changes before and after trade liberalization, allowing direct testing of whether free trade leads to domestic industry decline in these regions.

[PATH:theoretical] Rodrik, D. (2016). 'Premature deindustrialization'. Journal of Economic Growth, 21(1), 1-33. — Develops a theoretical framework explaining how trade liberalization in developing economies may lead to premature deindustrialization, offering testable predictions for the Southeast Asian and Sub-Saharan African context since the 1980s.

[PATH:empirical] UNIDO Industrial Statistics Database (INDSTAT2) and COMTRADE trade data for manufacturing sectors in Vietnam, Indonesia, Nigeria, and Kenya (1985-2015) — Enables comparative case-study analysis of domestic manufacturing output, employment, and import penetration trends, isolating the causal effect of free trade policies on domestic industry development.

C007.subject: free trade
C007.object: developing economies with robust anti-corruption measures
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: free trade developing economies with robust anti-corruption measures]

[PATH:empirical] World Bank Governance Indicators and trade openness panel data for sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia (2000-2020), linked to GDP growth rates — This allows a quantitative test of the interaction effect between free trade (measured by tariff reductions or trade-to-GDP ratio) and anti-corruption measures (e.g., Control of Corruption index) on economic growth, directly addressing the hypothesis in the specified regions and time period.

[PATH:literature] Rodrik, D. (2000). 'Trade Policy and Economic Growth: A Skeptic's Guide to the Cross-National Evidence' and subsequent meta-analyses — This foundational work and its follow-ups critically examine the conditions under which trade liberalization promotes growth, providing theoretical and empirical context for the role of institutional quality, including corruption control.

[PATH:theoretical] Acemoglu, D., & Robinson, J. A. (2012). 'Why Nations Fail: The Origins of Power, Prosperity, and Poverty' — This work offers a theoretical framework linking inclusive institutions (including anti-corruption) to the effectiveness of economic policies like free trade, helping to explain the hypothesized conditional relationship.

C008.subject: free trade
C008.object: developing economies regardless of institutional frameworks
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: free trade developing economies regardless of institutional frameworks]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative panel data analysis of Gini coefficients and trade openness indices (e.g., from World Bank WDI and UNU-WIDER) across Global South countries with varying institutional quality (e.g., rule of law, corruption indices) post-1980. — Directly tests the core claim by examining whether free trade correlates with increased inequality even when controlling for institutional frameworks, using cross-country time-series data.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing studies on trade liberalization and inequality in developing economies (e.g., from the Journal of International Economics or World Development), stratified by institutional quality measures. — Synthesizes prior findings to assess whether the pattern holds consistently across diverse institutional contexts, identifying potential moderators or contradictions.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical models of trade and inequality incorporating institutional frictions (e.g., extensions of the Stolper-Samuelson theorem with endogenous institutions or political economy constraints), published in top economics journals. — Provides causal mechanisms explaining why institutional frameworks might fail to mitigate inequality under free trade, offering a basis for empirical predictions and interpretation of results.
